`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes: 7 tests, all OK. I made two fixes in `household/bills.py` and changed one test expectation.

- **`split_bill`:** it dropped the leftover cents, so `split_bill(1001, 2)` returned `[500, 500]`. It now uses `divmod` and gives one extra cent each to the first `extra` people, as the docstring says.
- **`due_dates`:** the month number went past 12 when the dates crossed a year boundary, which caused the `IllegalMonthError` for month 13. It now rolls the year over correctly, so Dec 2026 is followed by Jan 2027.
- **`tests/test_bills.py` (your call):** `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3) == [333, 333, 333]`, which adds up to 999 cents. That contradicts both the docstring ("shares add up to exactly total_cents") and `test_remainder_goes_to_the_first`. I changed the expectation to `[334, 333, 333]`. If you meant the old behaviour, tell me and we can revisit it, but then the other test and the docstring would be wrong.
